build_runs: 6-page trial in the foreground: the build command without -d, with --limit 6 --workers 1; 6 pages read in 28.5 s

first full attempt with --workers 2 stopped after 2 pages: a worker process was killed (one OCR process measured about 3.5 GiB; Docker had 7.65 GiB shared with a running application stack). No manifest was written; the 2 pages it had written verified and were kept
final run: the build command above with --workers 1; 8 pages reused after verification, 492 read in 2016.8 s
verification: load_m4_cache(cache, dataset, verify='hashes') in the repository venv (Python 3.12, numpy 2, no Paddle): 500 pages; every cached file, the dataset manifest.csv and every source image match their recorded SHA-256
limitations: Synthetic pages only: this cache says nothing about OCR accuracy on real photographed estimates
OCR regions are text lines, not words
Three estimate pages are unreadable under M4's own nested-region rule and carry no text boxes; they are recorded as failed, not as empty pages
The working tree was dirty at build time; m4_source_sha256 identifies the M4 source that ran, the commit alone does not
PNG bytes depend on the OpenCV build, so a rebuild in another environment can give other rectified.png hashes for the same pixels
